profile.summary: FOAM (Formula-constrained Optimization for Annotating Metabolites) proposes molecular structures for an unknown tandem mass spectrum by optimisation rather than by a single trained generator. Given the spectrum and the molecular formula, it starts from seed structures with that formula, evolves them with a formula-constrained graph genetic algorithm, and keeps the candidates whose ICEBERG-simulated spectra best match the observed one. Seeds can come from PubChem or from other models such as DiffMS.

summary_quotes.text: Given an experimental spectrum and molecular formula, FOAM uses a formula-constrained graph genetic algorithm to propose and refine candidate structures, scoring them with ICEBERG (a learned spectral simulator) to maximize predicted spectral similarity to the observed spectrum.
FOAM supports the refinement of structures from any source---virtual libraries, generative models, or other domain-specific tools.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: FOAM first retrieves seed structures that match the formula (from PubChem, with the true structure excluded in evaluation, or from another tool). ICEBERG simulates the spectrum of each candidate, candidates are scored by similarity to the observed spectrum, and the best form a mating pool. A graph genetic algorithm then applies crossover and mutation that keep the formula fixed, and the loop repeats until a budget of ICEBERG calls is used. A multi-objective variant adds a penalty on structural complexity. FOAM has no trained weights of its own; the learned part is the ICEBERG simulator.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Reproduction configs are in configs/final, for NIST'20 (7,500 calls) and MassSpecGym with PubChem and DiffMS seeds. The MassSpecGym ICEBERG checkpoints (msg_gen.ckpt and msg_inten_cosine.ckpt) and the PubChem and DiffMS seed caches are on Zenodo record 18502041 (CC-BY-4.0, published 2026-02-06). The NIST'20 ICEBERG weights and NIST spectra are not public. A result should name the config, the seed sources, the call budget and the ICEBERG checkpoints.

sections.title: Use in the benchmark source
sections.body: MassSpecGym in the Wild (an existing source on this record) lists FOAM (DiffMS + PubChem) in its updated MassSpecGym de novo leaderboard with 1.50% top-1 accuracy. The FOAM paper added 100 DiffMS samples per spectrum to the seeds for MassSpecGym. It gives the MassSpecGym call budget as 5,000 in its results and 1,500 in its methods, and the repository's MassSpecGym config is named for 1,500 calls. The sources do not say which setting the leaderboard row used.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Optimisation workflow: formula-constrained graph genetic algorithm scored by a learned spectrum simulator (ICEBERG), for de novo structure elucidation.

quotes.text: FOAM couples a formula-constrained graph genetic algorithm with spectral simulation to explore candidate annotations given an experimental spectrum.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Graph genetic algorithm (crossover and mutation that keep the formula) with an ICEBERG oracle; optional multi-objective scoring.

facts.value: An experimental MS/MS spectrum (HDF5 or a folder of spectra) with its molecular formula, plus seed structures (HDF5 or a .txt of SMILES).

facts.value: Not applicable to FOAM itself, which is a search algorithm; the ICEBERG checkpoints it uses are separate models, and no parameter count for them is given in the sources read.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: FOAM is not trained. The MassSpecGym ICEBERG checkpoints are for MassSpecGym; a NIST'20 ICEBERG model trained on the commercial library is not public. Seeds come from PubChem formula matches and DiffMS samples.

facts.value: Single-objective and multi-objective modes; configs in configs/final for NIST'20 and MassSpecGym. No versioned releases are described.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not applicable; FOAM is not trained.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Not stated as a fixed limit; the search is bounded by the number of ICEBERG calls (--max-calls) and ICEBERG predicts up to --max-nodes fragments (100 in the demo).

strengths.text: Runs on CPU; the README times a 200-call demo at about 4 minutes on a 4-core desktop (the authors' figure).

limitations.text: Needs the molecular formula, and results depend on how close the seed structures are; the authors show success rises when a seed is structurally similar to the true molecule.

run_guide.summary: Install FOAM with ms-pred using uv, download the MassSpecGym ICEBERG checkpoints and seed caches from Zenodo, and run the MassSpecGym reproduction config.
prerequisites: At least 20 GB RAM; CPU is enough, an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.1 is optional.
About 20 GB of disk for data and checkpoints.
A MassSpecGym spectra HDF5 file, built with code in the ms-pred repository.

steps.title: Get the code and environment
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/coleygroup/foam.git
cd foam
git checkout --detach f3ed69b11642c01be0301dd2cfcba5cb3ee8c793
uv venv --python 3.10 ms-gen-foam
source ms-gen-foam/bin/activate
steps.explanation: As the README's uv route gives it; the checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit.

quotes.text: git clone https://github.com/coleygroup/foam.git cd foam uv venv --python 3.10 ms-gen-foam source ms-gen-foam/bin/activate

steps.title: Install ms-pred and FOAM
steps.shell:
cd .. && git clone https://github.com/coleygroup/ms-pred.git && cd ms-pred
git checkout fix-deps
uv pip install -e .
cd ../foam
uv pip install -e ".[cpu]"
steps.explanation: Installs ICEBERG's ms-pred package on its fix-deps branch, then FOAM for CPU; use .[cuda] for GPU.
